course_description_html:
Welcome back!  While optical switching currently solves spine layer and static topology challenges, research is advancing rapidly to handle dynamic workloads.

This module explores how emerging optical computing paradigms are shaping the future of data center infrastructure.

blocks.body_html:
We have examined how hyperscalers are currently utilizing optical switching to optimize static topologies and recover from physical hardware failures.

However, advanced artificial intelligence workloads are rarely static. The next evolution of data center networking must adapt in real time to the fluctuating demands of active compute phases.

blocks.heading_html: By the end of this module, you will be able to:

items_html: Describe three emerging OCS application areas: dynamic in-workload AI reconfiguration, Mixture-of-Experts training optimization, and quantum networking.
Explain the architectural innovations that make each of these applications possible.

blocks.quote_html: We want to extend our recognition to Ajay Gautham Manicka, Optical Transport Engineer at Nebius. His technical guidance was key during the design and development of this course.

blocks.body_html:
Current electrical designs lack the flexibility needed to support the highly dynamic communication patterns of modern AI workloads.

To address this, researchers developed the Adaptive Circuit Switching Techniques for AI Networking Architectures, or ACTINA.

ACTINA introduces a new topology called OCS-BCube. By enabling dynamically bandwidth steering, OCS-BCube delivers significantly faster iteration times compared to standard configurations.

Click the elements on the OCS-BCube diagram below to see how bandwidth is steered dynamically during training.

items.title: Multi-dimensional Connectivity
items.description_html: This design uses multi-dimensional connectivity tailored specifically for GPU-centric AI training clusters. It relies on a custom silicon photonics multi-port transceiver integrated directly into each GPU.

items.title: Silicon Photonic Transceivers
items.description_html: Each GPU houses a specialized module that dynamically reassigns wavelengths, enabling direct all-to-all optical connectivity.

items.title: Port Connectivity
items.description_html: The multi-dimensional design allows GPUs to communicate directly through the optical layer across different planes without electrical hops.

items.title: In-Workload Reconfiguration
items.description_html: The traffic-aware control plane changes wavelength assignments between iterations, shifting bandwidth to eliminate contention hotspots.

blocks.heading_html: Dynamic reconfiguration is also being applied to highly specialized training models like Mixture-of-Experts.

blocks.body_html:
Mixture-of-Experts training relies heavily on Expert Parallelism. This strategy requires massive and unpredictable all-to-all communication.

The following video demonstrates how the MixNet architecture isolates this traffic onto a dedicated optical layer.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.body_html: MixNet achieves its performance gains by splitting the cluster into three distinct interconnect fabrics, combining the strengths of electrical and optical switching.

items.title: Local Scale-Up Fabric
items.description_html: This electrical layer uses NVSwitch to provide high-bandwidth, low-latency communication for intra-server data transfers.

items.title: Global Scale-Out Fabric
items.description_html: This traditional EPS layer uses Ethernet or InfiniBand to connect servers across the cluster, handling predictable data and pipeline parallelism traffic.

items.title: Regional OCS Fabric
items.description_html: This purely optical layer is dedicated exclusively to Expert Parallelism. By recognizing that EP traffic is localized to groups of 8 to 32 GPUs and changes gradually, the system reconfigures this OCS layer during the compute phase so the links are ready before communication begins.

blocks.body_html: Lock in these emerging concepts using the flashcards below before we explore the final frontier of OCS applications.

blocks.heading_html: Beyond AI training, OCS is fundamentally enabling breakthroughs in both quantum networking and hardware disaggregation.

blocks.label: CONTINUE

blocks.body_html:
In quantum networks, information is carried by fragile quantum bits (qubits). The No-Cloning Theorem states that reading a quantum state destroys it. EPS switches, which convert and read packets for routing, cause immediate decoherence. In contrast, OCS is a transparent substrate that redirects photons, maintaining phase and polarization without collapsing the quantum state.

OCS also enables next-generation resource disaggregation. The following video details how removing OEO conversion preserves delicate quantum states and enables macro-level resource pooling.

blocks.heading_html: The exact properties that make OCS powerful for AI, makes it mandatory for quantum computing.

lessons.title: Knowledge Check
lessons.description_html:
Complete the knowledge check below to verify your understanding of these emerging OCS applications.

Select "Start Quiz" to begin.

blocks.question_html: What is the key reason conventional EPS networks are incompatible with quantum networking applications?

choices.text_html: They require OEO conversion which destroys qubit coherence

blocks.feedback_correct_html: Correct. EPS networks must convert and read packets, which measures the photon and collapses the delicate quantum state.
blocks.feedback_incorrect_html: Incorrect. Conventional EPS networks rely on OEO conversion, which destroys the quantum state of the qubits passing through them.

blocks.question_html: In MixNet, which parallelism strategy's communication patterns does the OCS regional fabric primarily serve?
blocks.feedback_correct_html: Correct. MixNet dedicates its highly reconfigurable regional OCS layer exclusively to the heavy, localized traffic of Expert Parallelism.
blocks.feedback_incorrect_html: Incorrect. The regional OCS fabric in MixNet is designed specifically to handle Expert Parallelism.

blocks.question_html: ACTINA's OCS-BCube achieves better tokens-per-joule compared to alternatives primarily through which architectural mechanism?
blocks.feedback_correct_html: Correct. The custom silicon-photonics MZI modules allow the system to dynamically steer bandwidth in real time during a workload, significantly improving efficiency.
blocks.feedback_incorrect_html: Incorrect. OCS-BCube utilizes wavelength-reconfigurable transceivers to steer bandwidth dynamically during active workloads.

blocks.body_html: Great job! Having explored both current production models and the future frontier of optical networking, let's have a look at the main takeaways from the technologies and applications we explored in this module:

items_html: ACTINA and OCS-BCube enable dynamic, in-workload bandwidth steering using custom silicon-photonics transceivers, accelerating iteration times.
MixNet isolates Expert Parallelism traffic onto a dedicated regional OCS layer, predicting traffic patterns and reconfiguring optical links during the compute phase.
OCS acts as a transparent substrate vital for quantum networking because it preserves qubit states by completely avoiding OEO conversion.
Rate-agnostic optical links enable resource disaggregation by eliminating queuing latency between pooled hardware.

blocks.heading_html: We will conclude the course by examining the broader industry ecosystem and your role within the OCP community.
